documents.unit: Center for Teaching Excellence (approved by Office of Academic Affairs)
documents.title: Syllabus Statements to Address the Usage of Artificial Intelligence in the Classroom
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university rule: 'Faculty are encouraged to add one of the three sample statements' and each sample begins 'For instructors who choose to' permit, limit or prohibit, so the decision is delegated and the three options are listed as tiers.
documents.summary: A Center for Teaching Excellence page offering three Academic Affairs-approved sample syllabus statements (permit with citation, limited use on select assignments, prohibit). Faculty choose one; the university sets no default and invites faculty to share their own statements.

units.why: The page tells faculty to add one of three Academic Affairs-approved sample statements; they are 'encouraged' but not required, so the phase is before-course and the modality 'should'. P09 fits best because it concerns stating AI expectations in the syllabus, though here it is encouraged rather than mandatory.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to add one of the three sample statements below to their syllabi
units.frag_start: Faculty are encouraged to add
units.frag_end: Office of Academic Affairs has approved.
units.fit_note: The statement is encouraged, not mandatory.

units.why: The three samples let each instructor choose a stance: 'For instructors who choose to' embrace, allow limited use, or prohibit. This delegates the decision to the instructor (P04); P05 is a close alternative, but the options are sample statements, not defined tiers of use.
units.anchor: For instructors who choose to
units.frag_start: For instructors who choose to
units.policy: Instructors choose among permitting, limiting or prohibiting ChatGPT or other AI generative software in their courses.

units.why: The page labels three named options, 'EMBRACE/PERMIT', 'LIMITED/SELECT USAGE' and 'PROHIBIT/EXCLUDE', so P05 fits best as a set of named categories, even though they are sample statements for instructors and not tiers students are placed in.
units.anchor: EMBRACE/PERMIT
units.frag_start: EMBRACE/PERMIT
units.policy: The university offers three named options for syllabus statements: embrace/permit, limited/select usage, and prohibit/exclude.
units.fit_note: Options are sample statements for instructors, not tiers students are placed in.

units.why: The invitation to share statements and assignment language with CTE to 'build a repository' is a faculty-support and community mechanism, not a rule about student AI use; P63 fits since the CTE collects and supports instructors' policies.
units.anchor: faculty are invited to share their AI-related syllabus statements
units.frag_start: These are suggested syllabus statements
units.fit_note: Sharing builds a repository; no training or workshops are mentioned.

units.why: The permit sample says ChatGPT 'may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation', a default permission with a citation condition, so permit with may, in the P02 default-permit category.

units.policy: Students cite AI use appropriately when using AI language models on assignments.

units.why: 'You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI Generative Software' puts verification on the student, matching P31 (verify AI output) rather than P29, because it is about checking accuracy of AI text.

units.why: The permit sample opens by praising ChatGPT: it 'offers an innovative and effective approach to education, enhancing both teaching and learning'. It is a rationale for allowing AI as beneficial; P44 is the nearest type, with a fit note.

units.fit_note: Claims educational benefit, not employer-expected professional skill.

units.why: The limited sample says ChatGPT 'should be used selectively and thoughtfully', a soft norm to restrict use. P03 (discourage without forbidding) is chosen over P04 because it is a general cautious norm, not a decision about who sets the rule.

units.why: 'serves as a supplementary tool rather than a replacement for human interaction' gives the reason for limiting use: AI should supplement, not replace, people. P72 is the nearest type because it concerns human support alongside AI, but nobody is directed to human help.

units.why: 'may be used on select assignments in this course, as defined by the instructor' permits AI only on assignments the instructor designates, so the rule is assignment-level and instructor-defined: P04. It is restrict because use is allowed only where designated.

notes: Single university-layer page; no computing or school policy found. Course syllabi deferred. The limited-sample fact-checking duty repeats the permit-sample duty in a different option; kept as a separate unit.
